scope: Local systems-language toolchain, Python reference runtime, experimental native C17 compiler track, Studio, stdio LSP/DAP and explicit local integrations; not a hosted backend service.

status_policy.rule: Use implemented or partial only when repository code and focused verification paths support the exact statement. Record limits explicitly. A design document, capability catalog or profile-validation job does not prove runtime behavior.

controls.title: Module boundaries and versioned contracts
controls.assessment: The language modules, runtime APIs and transactional snapshot contract define explicit component boundaries; cross-file semantic and ABI guarantees remain staged.
limitations: Module and host APIs are not a claim of a fully native compiler/runtime or stable external ABI.

controls.title: Input validation and idempotent state changes
controls.assessment: Frontend quotas, parser checks and optimistic transaction generations bound and protect selected state-changing operations.
limitations: The Python reference runtime remains the compatibility implementation; idempotency is provided only where the operation contract defines it.

controls.title: Low-level I/O and transport boundaries
controls.assessment: LSP and DAP expose local stdio protocol adapters with protocol-focused tests; a remote network service is not part of the current product scope.
limitations: Stdio protocol support does not establish a network daemon, remote execution or distributed transport.

controls.title: Concurrency, scheduling and backpressure
controls.assessment: The project has local runtime and tooling paths, but bounded worker scheduling, queue saturation and cancellation behavior have not been established as a general runtime contract.
limitations: Do not infer concurrency safety or load capacity from asynchronous API names or local process boundaries.

controls.title: Memory ownership and resource lifetime
controls.assessment: The runtime includes explicit memory and execution-budget components with focused regression coverage.
limitations: These controls do not establish native ownership checking, a general allocator, or cross-process memory isolation.

controls.title: Data integrity and transactions
controls.assessment: RuntimeTransaction uses bounded JSON-compatible snapshots, generations, digests and rollback for caller-owned in-memory state.
limitations: The transaction API is not a persistent database transaction or firmware-flashing facility.

controls.title: Failure handling, recovery and lifecycle
controls.assessment: The resilience policy and transaction tests specify bounded retries, safe failures and rollback for selected local operations.
limitations: A validated policy file does not enforce every runtime failure path; no distributed recovery system is claimed.

controls.title: Security, privileges and secret handling
controls.assessment: Execution audit and local trust-boundary guidance exist, with tests for audit behavior and resilience-policy invariants.
limitations: The local interpreter is not a sandbox for hostile native code; no hosted identity or secret service is claimed.

controls.title: Observability and diagnostics
controls.assessment: The runtime exposes audit records and structured diagnostics for selected execution and toolchain operations.
limitations: There is no distributed tracing or service-level latency telemetry for the current local product.

controls.title: Performance budgets and capacity
controls.assessment: No verified service throughput, queue-capacity or horizontal scaling baseline is currently defined for the local language toolchain.
limitations: Do not claim horizontal scalability or production server capacity for a local CLI and desktop IDE.

controls.title: Configuration, extensibility and integration
controls.assessment: Plugin and Kora module interfaces provide explicit local extension points and dedicated compatibility tests.
limitations: Plugin discovery is not permission to execute untrusted code; extension sandboxing remains a separate requirement.

controls.title: Verification and delivery gate
controls.assessment: This PR adds a machine-readable backend engineering profile, safe-path/status validator, negative self-tests and a dedicated CI gate.
limitations: The gate validates profile integrity and evidence paths; it does not certify compiler parity, native runtime completeness or production readiness.
